subject.title: gateway install/status hardcodes ~/Library/LaunchAgents — prevents boot-without-login on macOS

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class macOS system LaunchDaemon gateway support, and what exact scope flag, sudo behavior, execution user, status semantics, and lifecycle coverage should it own?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix because it creates a privileged service mode and changes managed gateway ownership, operator recovery, and security expectations on macOS.

options.title: Add explicit system mode
options.body: Keep LaunchAgent as the default and add an audited LaunchDaemon path covering install/status/lifecycle, `UserName`, durable environment handling, doctor repair, docs, and tests.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Improve status/doctor/install guidance so custom LaunchDaemons are detected and duplicate user installs are refused while keeping LaunchDaemon installation outside the shipped CLI.

options.title: Keep external only
options.body: Document custom LaunchDaemon ownership as unsupported core behavior and close or park the feature direction after preserving the related evidence.

recommendation.title: Add explicit system mode
recommendation.body: Keep LaunchAgent as the default and add an audited LaunchDaemon path covering install/status/lifecycle, `UserName`, durable environment handling, doctor repair, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal on the launchd/path helper boundary and this decision cuts across CLI, gateway service lifecycle, and security UX.
